Title: Detecting Violation of Human Rights via Social Media
Author(s): Yash Pilankar, Rejwanul Haque, et al.
Dataset: Manually created dataset of Twitter posts on human rights violations
Implementation: Classification models to identify factual tweets on human rights violation
Conclusion: Model achieved 93% accuracy identifying human rights violation tweets; useful for real-time monitoring
Future Scope: Extend dataset size; enhance multilingual detection; apply to other social media platforms

Title: Social Media and Human Rights - Issues raised by online social media for political activism
Dataset: Various social media and online activism data
Implementation: Discussion paper on political activism, censorship, and online surveillance
Conclusion: Online social media is a double-edged sword for political rights; enabling activism but inviting repression
Future Scope: Develop better regulation balancing free speech and government control; novel tech for transparency

Title: Impact of Social Media on Geopolitics and Economic Growth
Dataset: Social media usage statistics and geopolitical data
Implementation: Examines economic consequences linked to social media in geopolitics
Conclusion: Social media influences economic growth but also facilitates economic rights violations via misinformation and manipulation
Future Scope: Further empirical studies on economic impact and rights protection strategies

Title: Tanzania youth and social media: perceptions, experiences and implications for human rights violations
Dataset: Focus group discussions and in-depth interviews with youth
Implementation: Analysis of misuse of social media by youth leading to rights violations
Conclusion: Youth misuse for financial gain, peer pressure causes privacy invasion & abuse; women and children vulnerable
Future Scope: Awareness programs for youth; educational interventions on ethical ICT use

Title: Exploring Social Media Privacy Concerns
Dataset: Census-representative online panel survey in 16 MENA countries
Implementation: Analysis of multi-level social media privacy concerns across culturally diverse populations
Conclusion: Cultural norms strongly influence privacy concerns; social media privacy violations have cultural dimensions in MENA region
Future Scope: Expand research to other regions; develop culturally aware privacy protections
